//: THE measured settle table.  ONE copy, read by three things:
//2: set_brake against the release time recorded here;
//3: - the [Runway] coverage guard, which requires every abs_*.json that
//4: gates a brake behind a wait_for_speed barrier to appear here;
//6: fields from a headless run and fails when they disagree.
//8: WHY A DATA FILE.  Until 2026-08-12 this table was a C++ array in
//9: tests/test_scenario.cpp, so nothing outside the test binary could read
//10: it, and re-deriving the numbers meant a human running the report and
//11: eyeballing seven pairs.  Nobody did that on a schedule, and the table
//12: carried a phantom 12.011 s for abs_brake_and_steer that no tool had
//13: ever produced.  A second copy in the report script would have been the
//14: same defect one file over, so there is exactly one copy: this file.
//16: MEASURED vs REQUIRED — the distinction the whole file turns on.
//17: measured_release_s, measured_crossing_s are OBSERVATIONS of the
//18: plant.  They move when the powertrain, the tyre, the mass or the
//19: throttle ramp moves (the 2026-08-11 motor corner correction shifted
//20: every one of them ~3 % later).  Re-derive them, never hand-edit:
//22: min_settle_s, min_on_surface_s are REQUIREMENTS we chose.  Nothing
//23: re-derives those; changing one is a decision, not a measurement.
//25: wait_for_speed is a barrier (src/Scenario.cpp): it does not advance the
//26: event index, so every later event whose at_time_s has already passed
//27: fires on the tick the barrier releases.  A set_brake at 6.0 s behind a
//28: barrier releasing at 7.7 s applies full brake at 7.7 s with the
//29: drivetrain still loaded and launch slip still in the tyres.  That is why
//30: a scenario's own at_time_s cannot answer the question and a measurement
//33: 2026-10-08: the six VAT ABS stops (high_mu, low_mu, mu_jump, split_mu,
//34: brake_and_steer, diagonal_mu) left this table.  They now start rolling
//35: (spawn.speed_mps in their configs) and have no barrier; their brake
//36: is guarded against the electronics boot by the [Runway] case
//37: "every rolling-start ABS scenario brakes after the electronics boot".

tolerances.//: How far a re-derived number may sit from the one recorded here.
tolerances.//1: The plant is deterministic — two runs of the same binary produce
tolerances.//2: byte-identical stats CSVs — so a disagreement is a real movement,
tolerances.//3: not noise, and these could in principle be a millisecond.  They are
tolerances.//4: not, because a Chrono or compiler change may legitimately move the
tolerances.//5: last digit.  What they must be is far tighter than the slack the
tolerances.//6: [Runway] cases run on: the tightest settle is 2.96 s against a 2.0 s
tolerances.//7: requirement, so 0.96 s of drift would eat the settle while every
tolerances.//8: assertion stayed green.  0.05 s catches that 19x over.
tolerances.//9: release_s is read from the scenario log (millisecond resolution);
tolerances.//10: crossing_s is read from the stats CSV, whose sample period is 0.02 s
tolerances.//11: for all seven, so its floor is a couple of samples rather than a ms.
